flows.narrative: Lipper's week-to-26-Aug data shows the first crack in an otherwise resilient inflow picture: global equity funds posted a -$5.87bn outflow, snapping 13 consecutive weeks of inflows, with US equity funds specifically seeing -$22.33bn in net sales -- the primary drag. This run located Lipper's fuller regional split for the same week, superseding the smaller/differently-scoped BofA-EPFR 'featured week' figures used previously: Europe equity funds actually drew a solid +$7.92bn inflow (not the +$55mn figure previously cited from a different EPFR cut), Asia equity funds +$4.8bn, EM equity funds +$709mn (a 7th consecutive week of inflows, updating the prior week's +$1.57bn/6th-week figure), and EM bond funds +$956mn -- so the outflow was concentrated specifically in the US, not global. Also newly found: money-market funds saw a -$19.74bn outflow the same week, ending a 4-week inflow streak -- a genuinely fresh data point not previously captured, sitting alongside gold/precious-metals funds' +$4.21bn (6-month high) and short-term bond funds' +$6.29bn (7-week high), consistent with a rotation out of both US equities AND cash into gold/duration ahead of Friday's Warsh shock. Global bond funds added a slower +$10.25bn (a 4-week-low pace). BofA's Flow Show cross-check (older, ~22 Aug featured week) showed the same defensive tilt at larger EPFR-scope magnitudes: gold funds +$6.3bn (biggest since Jan 2026), tech funds' first outflow in 6 weeks (-$700mn), and the Bull & Bear Indicator at 9.7 (highest since 2021, contrarian 'sell' territory) -- not re-verified fresher this run. Separately, BofA/EPFR crypto-fund flows (outside this file's regional scope) swung sharply: +$3.2bn for the week to ~22 Aug (strongest since Oct 2025, ~81% BTC/ETH ETFs) before cooling to +$924.5mn for 24-28 Aug. Japan drew a 9th straight week of fund inflows (+$2.6bn) even as JPX's own data (see flows-investors.json) shows foreign investors net-SELLING Japanese cash equities -- a genuine flow-vs-fund-positioning divergence tied to the JGB yield surge.
